 Damian Lillard had an ad of his own. It went down back in 2014, when the Portland Trail Blazers point guard teamed up with Foot Locker.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Lillard's early confidence 
 At the time , Lillard had just finished his second NBA season. And what a start it was.
 He won the ROY award over players like Anthony Davis and Bradley Beal. In year two, he was already an All-Star. Over his first two campaigns, Dame averaged 19.9 points, 3.3 rebounds and 6.1 assists.
 Numbers like that bring attention. Lillard got his share. It was also a big reason he landed his first national TV commercial.
 The plot of "No Rings" ?
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Dame walks into a living room where a few guys are on the couch watching basketball. He joins them. He's on the phone with a buddy, carrying a Foot Locker bag. Still talking, he reveals he just picked up "some new Adidas gear." 
 Why? Because when you look good, you play good, Lillard explains.
 The camera cuts to a closer shot. The future nine-time All-Star then says something he'd clearly set his mind on.
 "The last thing I wanna be," Lillard emphasizes, "is one of those guys who never won a ring." 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement A star-studded twist 
 After Lillard shares that goal, the camera pans to the guys next to him.
 Turns out they're Barry Sanders and LaDainian Tomlinson. NFL legends. Neither won a Super Bowl, though. So they're clearly baffled.
 Sanders says, "Wow." Tomlinson simply throws both hands up.
 Dame catches the drift. He quickly clarifies that he only means "basketball players who never won a ring." 
 Good enough. Until the camera switches to the other side of the room.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Chris Webber is sitting there. He is, in fact, a "basketball player who never won a ring." Now he feels called out, shooting the reigning All-Star a disgusted look.
 A laughing Lillard has another excuse ready, though. He is actually talking about "one of those legends who lost in the Finals over and over." 
 The twist?
 Before he can catch his breath, Dame looks out the window. Karl Malone , who clearly fits the description, stands there. Looking disappointed, The Mailman has been at the grill outside. All he can manage is, "Burgers are ready." 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The oldest MVP in league history then shuffles back into the dining room, head down. Sanders, meanwhile, calls him back.
 Related: "Can you put me in a headlock?" – Sophie Cunningham reveals bizarre requests she gets from WNBA fans 
 The irony 
 The plot is as funny as it gets. It's also clear why they chose Lillard for it. At the time, he was seen as someone who'd definitely avoid ending up ringless. He, in fact, had just led his franchise back to the playoffs.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Still, Lillard will likely go down as one of those guys himself. At 36 and in his 14th NBA season, he still hasn't won a ring. Now back with the Blazers, they aren't seen as true contenders, either.
 When Dame eventually calls it quits without a ring, a remake of that commercial might be hilarious, though. Only this time, he'd play the other role. For that, the 2024 NBA Cup champion would definitely need a little gallows humor.
